articles.title: Why Two Man Utd Talents Have Joined Arsenal in the Last Two Days
articles.excerpt: The Gunners have deliberately recruited several young players with first-team ambitions.
articles.content:
This weekend, Arsenal signed James Scanlon from Manchester United on Saturday and then announced the capture of Habeeb Ogunneye, also from the Red Devils, on Sunday.

It is part of a targeted approach from the Gunners this summer to strengthen at the academy level, with five such players recruited in the last five days alone.

Scanlon, who turns 20 next month, and Ogunneye, 21 in November, are talents who will hope to join on the fringes of the first team and soon make that breakthrough. Neither ever made a first-team appearance for Manchester United, although both did get on the senior bench and both gained first-team experience in the EFL League Two during loans last season.

It is a reversal of the transfer that saw an 18-year-old Ayden Heaven leave Arsenal for Manchester United in January 2025 in the hope of a clearer pathway. The center back has since played 25 senior matches and appears to have a bright future, which so far vindicates the decision to switch clubs in the hope of furthering his career.

Arsenal Sign Left-Wing Prospect

Scanlon was born and raised in England’s East Midlands, having been in Derby County’s academy before moving to Manchester aged 14, but appears to be motivated by Arsenal’s recent Premier League success and the upward trajectory of the club.

“I think you can see where the club’s at, [it’s] really positive and I think it’s only going to get better,” the teenager told Arsenal’s in-house media.

“You can see that everyone here is hungrier for more, hungrier to get better and I think that’s something I believe I can add to and want to be a part of as well.”

With Arsenal struggling to recruit another left winger this summer but in the process of selling Gabriel Martinelli to Al Hilal, there is potentially a direct path into the first team for Scanlon, who plays on the left or as a No. 10. The youngster, who already has 24 international caps for Gibraltar, describes himself as a “creative player” who likes to “score goals, assist.”

Arsenal’s Recent Youth Development Stands Out

Ogunneye is originally from London and so has a clear family connection to the city, although his association with Manchester United lasted 15 years—most of his young life.

The defender is specifically a right back and said upon joining the club that he hopes Arsenal’s production line will serve him as it has done others in recent years.

"When I heard [Arsenal] were interested in me, I said to my agents it’s a no-brainer,” Ogunneye explained. “Seeing all the young players that are coming through as well, I just wanted to come straight away. I just wanted to be part of that group, and win games together. It’s good playing with good players, good defenders; it’s only going to better you.”

Myles Lewis-Skelly, Max Dowman and Ethan Nwaneri have all made the jump from Arsenal’s Hale End academy to the first team in the past few seasons. Bukayo Saka was also only 18 years old when he started regularly playing for the senior squad in 2019.

In Ogunneye’s position there initially appears to be more immediate competition than Scanlon might face, with Jurriën Timber and Ben White the primary right backs. Cristhian Mosquera and Ezri Konsa can also play the position, although both are seen as center backs first.

It’s worth noting, however, that Timber is currently sidelined and has been injured for a cumulative 443 days since joining in 2023. White has also often been linked with an exit since losing his starting place, and Ogunneye might not be that far away from an opportunity. 

Jamie Spencer is a writer and editor for SI FC. Jamie grew up in Manchester, England, in the 1990s and fell in love with the game at the same time as the Premier League was taking off. With more than a decade of experience behind him in sports media, he specializes in Manchester United and the overall Premier League, still living in England’s north-west soccer hotbed. Jamie is also an expert on the women’s game and enjoys old school nostalgia, telling stories from soccer’s rich history and culture.

articles.title: Vigil review – this police thriller is twisty, explosive … and so boring
articles.excerpt: Suranne Jones and Rose Leslie are back trying to stop a third world war in the Arctic. There’s plenty of action – but it’s hard to root for heroes whose biggest personality traits are ‘being nice’ and ‘wears good glasses
articles.content:
Suranne Jones and Rose Leslie are back trying to stop a third world war in the Arctic. There’s plenty of action – but it’s hard to root for heroes whose biggest personality traits are ‘being nice’ and ‘wears good glasses’

Like many a police procedural, Vigil always begins with a cold open. This time round, however, it’s absolutely freezing. We are, as per, thrown headlong into a niche and tangentially Scottish military world where a murder has occurred. The first series took place on board a nuclear submarine (the show is, confusingly, still named after the vessel), while the second split the action between an army airfield in Scotland and the fictional Middle Eastern nation of Wudyan.

For its third outing, we find ourselves in the (real) Arctic region of Svalbard. The area is supposedly demilitarised, but four British special forces agents are working undercover at a research centre, and tonight their mission is to extract a Chinese scientist who has made a discovery that could either save or destroy the world. En route, they’re ambushed by Russians who want whatever world-saving-or-destroying stuff she’s got. The scientist escapes – but one of the Brits later turns up dead in a Russian enclave.

The action moves from (slightly less) snowcapped (than they used to be) mountains to the snuggly Glasgow bedroom of Vigil’s police protagonists: DCI Amy Silva (Suranne Jones) and her colleague and girlfriend DI Kirsten Longacre (Rose Leslie), who has spent the past year looking after the pair’s baby son, Fergal. As far as I can gather, Silva and Longacre are relatively run-of-the-mill detectives, yet Vigil relies on them being assigned to cases that could feasibly trigger a third world war on at least an annual basis. You know when people say returning to work after maternity leave feels like a nice break from relentless childcare? I don’t think that applies when your first day back involves flying nearly to the north pole to investigate a murder while ensuring the UK avoids an international incident with Russia. But at least Longacre gets some peace and quiet on the plane.

Silva, to her slight chagrin, is ordered to stay on home turf. Little does she know that’s where the explosive drama is. It’s climate conference season and a Scottish scientist has flown back from Svalbard with suspicious haste for the occasion. Moments after Silva doorsteps him at his university, he is blown up by a bomb in his lab. As she enters, another man runs out – a climate activist with a rather convoluted grudge.

In the Arctic, meanwhile, the violence is more psychological. In order to keep the peace, Svalbard’s Norwegian police chief must treat Russian and UK representatives with strict equality. That means the Russians are permitted to appoint their own detective, Col Zamorin, to the investigation. But is he friend or foe? And who will find the Chinese scientist and her mysterious grail first?

Vigil is, obviously, not your standard murder mystery – each series is set on the precipice of an alarmingly realistic geopolitical crisis. The second series revolved around the sale of British arms to the Middle East; this time themes include Russian expansionism, our age of trollish diplomacy and how the interests of the global energy industry trump concerns about the climate crisis (PS: we’re doomed). Playing out over this chaotic backdrop of current affairs is a stream of individual deceptions: pretty much every character is harbouring a major secret. Like a global Line of Duty, this is essentially a programme about not being able to trust a soul in the police, the intelligence services or the military. Far from being a guarantee against criminality, rank is probably a confirmation of it.

Wanton complexity isn’t always a bad thing in a thriller, especially in the age of second screening-related simplicity. The problem is that Vigil’s twist-rate is too high for any revelation to effectively land. The levels of conspiracy are flummoxing and seemingly never-ending: just as one layer of lies has been peeled off, we’re confronted by another. The capacity to be surprised is stripped away in the process.

If you can’t invest in the case, you need to be able to invest in the leads. Unfortunately, this is Vigil’s weakest link. Silva is essentially a blank slate: the closest thing she has to a personality trait is putting on and swiftly taking off a massive pair of reading glasses. Leslie assumes a very broad Glaswegian accent to play Longacre, whose defining characteristic is that she’s … quite nice? Not to suggest Silva isn’t also quite nice – she is! The pair’s working relationship is not impeded by their romantic one, either. They are both too sensible and professional for their (mild) domestic friction to tip over into popcorn-crunching drama.

Instead, what we’re left with is a mystery designed to wrongfoot the viewer to a tedious degree, which plays out over a backdrop of urgent real-world jeopardy. Unfortunately, those two things end up cancelling each other out. Vigil makes it hard to keep caring, even when it’s the planet’s future that is at stake.

Vigil is on BBC One and iPlayer in the UK and SBS and SBS on Demand in Australia.

articles.title: Vigil season 3 cast: Meet the new and returning characters of gripping BBC drama
articles.excerpt: Want to know who is joining Suranne Jones and Rose Leslie for Vigil season three? Here's all the new and returning cast and characters for Vigil season three.
articles.content:
Who is joining Suranne Jones and Rose Leslie?

Jump to:

  • Vigil season three returning cast and characters
  • Vigil season three new cast and characters
  • Vigil season three full cast and characters

Need something to make you feel a bit better about the fact that summer is basically over? Well, my friend, this is it: Vigil will return to screens for a third season very soon. Yay!

The gripping crime series — which follows military investigator DCI Amy Silva as she investigates mysterious deaths and high-level military conspiracies — returns to BBC for season three this weekend. When, I hear you ask? Episode one airs on BBC One at 9pm on Sunday 30 August. The six-part series will then roll out across three weeks, with two episodes a week (on Sundays and Mondays). You'll also be able to stream the series on BBC iPlayer.

As for what the third instalment of Vigil is about? According to a BBC synopsis, season three will see DCI Silva (along with DI Kirsten Longacre) head to a remote Arctic research station, where a member of a covert British special forces mission has been murdered.

The synopsis goes on: "Amy and Kirsten need to catch the killer and defuse a potential international confrontation, as different nations compete for control of the Arctic and its resources in the changing polar climate, with both their careers and relationship on the line."

So, who can viewers expect to see in this Arctic edition of Vigil? Here's all the information on the full cast and character list for Vigil season three...

Vigil season three returning cast and characters

Suranne Jones as DCI Amy Silva

Who is Amy? Amy has been the lead character of Vigil since season one. In season three, she has to work a new case that's unfolding in the Arctic. Per the BBC, Amy is "is feisty, she's a maverick, she's straight talking, she has a really good heart and a strong belief for the need for the world to be good."

What else has Suranne Jones been in? Doctor Foster, Hostage, Gentleman Jack, Frauds, Save Me, Unforgiven.

Rose Leslie as DI Kirsten Longacre

Who is Kirsten? Kirsten is Amy's partner – in both work and life. She joined the show in season two, and recently gave birth to their child. In season three, she travels to Svalbard in the Arctic to crack their latest case. According to the BBC, Kirsten is a "strong-willed, tenacious police officer who is loyal but also very passionate about her job."

What else has Rose Leslie been in? Game of Thrones, The Time Traveller's Wife, Death on the Nile, Miss Austen, The Hack.

Gary Lewis as DSU Colin Robertson

Who is Colin? DSU Colin Robertson is one of the few returning characters in Vigil, working alongside Amy and Kirsten.

What else has Gary Lewis been in? Billy Elliot, Outlander, My Son.

Dominic Mafham as Sir Ian Downing

Who is Ian? Sir Ian Downing – who appeared in Vigil season two – is a high-ranking MI5 official.

What else has Dominic Mafham been in? Grantchester, Coronation Street, The Marlow Murder Club.

Vigil season three new cast and characters

Jeppe Beck Laursen as Henrik Becken

Who is Henrik? "Henrik Becken is the Director of Svalbard and Chief of Police, so he gets very involved in the investigation," the BBC explains. "He's working closely with Kirsten and Amy, as well as Fyodor, the Russian Colonel."

What else has Jeppe Beck Laursen been in? The Last King, Cold Feet.

Tornike Gogrichiani as Fyodor

Who is Fyodor? "Fyodor is a Russian colonel who arrives in Svalbard to investigate the murder of the Russian citizen and British soldier who was found dead in a Russian-owned building," the BBC notes. "He works closely Kirsten and Amy on the investigation."

What else has Tornike Gogrichiani been in? Extraction 2, Drops of God.

Naomi Yang as Shen Jia

Who is Shen? Shen Jia is a microbiologist conducting research on Svalbard. "She has very strong values and won't compromise those even when things get tough," the actor who plays her told the BBC. "She's someone with a lot of integrity."

What else has Naomi Yang been in? Brassic, Peaky Blinders, Grace, Under Salt Marsh.

Steven Miller as Mark Cunningham

Who is Mark? Mark Cunningham is a Special Boat Service operator.

What else has Steven Miller been in? Father Brown, Casualty, The Walk-In, Dept. Q, Shetland.

Benjamin Wainwright as Oli Pickford

Who is Oli? Like Mark, Oli Pickford is a Special Boat Service operator.

What else has Benjamin Wainwright been in? The Split, Gangs of London, Halo.

Danusia Samal as Jasmine Kelly

Who is Jasmine? Jasmine Kelly works at MI5 with Sir Ian Downing.

What else has Danusia Samal been in? The Great, Gangs of London, Red Eye.

Shereen Cutkelvin plays Holly Mitchell

Who is Holly? Holly is a DS working with Amy and the team at their Scottish base.

What else has Shereen Cutkelvin been in? Saturday Mash-Up, Summerwater.

Vigil season three full cast and characters

  • Suranne Jones as Amy Silva
  • Rose Leslie as Kirsten Longacre
  • Gary Lewis as Colin Robertson
  • Dominic Mafham as Sir Ian Downing
  • Jeppe Beck Laursen as Henrick Becken
  • Tornike Gogrichiani as Fyodor
  • Naomi Yang as Shen Jia
  • Steven Miller as Mark Cunningham
  • Benjamin Wainwright as Oli Pickford
  • Danusia Samal as Jasmine Kelly
  • Jordan Duvigneau as Simon Anderson
  • Eric Godon as Mayor Korotayev
  • Orla Russell as Poppy Silva
  • Amy Manson as Lorna McCallister
  • Artur Zai Barrera as Garcia
  • Jason Tobin as Huang Chen
  • Shereen Cutkelvin as Holly Mitchell
  • Kaisa Hammarlund as Deputy Olsdatter
  • Adam Fidusiewicz as Evgeni
  • Conor Berry as Daniel Hodge
  • Steven Cree as Gordon Laity
  • Killian Coyle as Jason Collyer
  • Derek Riddell as Vincent Mair
  • Alma Prelec as Polina
  • Dawn Sievewright as Chloe Ackroyd

Watch Vigil season three on BBC One and BBC iPlayer from Sunday 30 August.
